content:
alex_s: Heads-up — customer reported a big invoice jump. SDK estimator (client) shows ~1.2k tokens for the session, invoice shows ~6.1k. Repro looks like it happens when streaming connections reconnect/resume. Anyone seen this? :thinking:

mei_l: I think I've seen similar. Streaming reconnects can trigger a server-side prefix re-injection. Does the SDK re-send system messages on resume?

alex_s: Minimal repro below. Using our JS streaming helper. Estimate at client end = 1.2k, server metering logs show ~6k tokens.

alex_s: ```js
// pseudocode repro (client)
const s = stream.open({ model: 'redwood-lite', system: 'You are an assistant' });
s.send('Prompt part 1');
// simulate network blip, reconnect
s.close();
await sleep(200);
const s2 = stream.open({ model: 'redwood-lite', system: 'You are an assistant' });
s2.send('Prompt part 2');
// client estimator only counts the visible prompt/completion tokens
```

jordan_p: Quick guess: when stream reopens server-side may append the system/tool preamble again for safety (to reconstruct context), and metering counts that full preamble each time. Client estimator probably doesn't because it only counts what it sent on the wire.

mei_l: That matches the logs I pulled earlier. From metering pipeline: 
```
metering: session=rs-42 stream_id=abc tokens_counted=6127 events=[sys_preamble: 3x(512 tok), user_chunk: 2x(256 tok), tool_metadata: 1x(128 tok)]
```
Server shows system preamble counted 3x (reconnects) while client only sent it once in perceived conversation.

alex_s: The subtle part: SDK attempts to be helpful and *doesn't* resend system message on resume (so client estimate stays low). But runtime inserts the preamble again to ensure stateless consumers have context. Metering counts what runtime executes.

metering-bot: ALERT account=r-0xx spike=4.9x period=hour reason=unusual_token_pattern link=/billing/invoice/r-0xx/2026-02

jordan_p: Repro steps I recommend to validate quickly: 
1) Start stream with system. record client estimator.
2) Force TCP drop/close, reopen new stream without sending system.
3) Capture server metering logs (stream/session id).
4) Compare token deltas and look for repeated preamble counts.

alex_s: I ran that and attached logs. Key evidence: server metering shows extra 512-token chunks labeled `sys_preamble` with same content hash. Client-side estimator shows only user tokens + completion.

mei_l: Two action items: (1) eng-runtime: consider dedupe by session_id + preamble hash on reconnection when the same model+system text is present; (2) metrics: expose a breakdown in console that surfaces repeated preamble counts so customers can debug.

jordan_p: Also worth checking tool calls: if a tool runs on reconnect the runtime may re-emit tool metadata (headers/payload) which is non-trivial token cost. I saw `tool_metadata` once in logs.

alex_s: For immediate customer triage: offered credits for the delta and asked them to send exact sequence of reconnects. They provided timestamps that align with three reconnects in a 7-minute window.

mei_l: Small mitigation we can ship quickly: do not double-count preamble tokens in metering if the session indicates a continuation and the preamble hash matches previous. Need eng-runtime signoff.

jordan_p: I'll open an internal issue with runtime tracing info + sample logs. Assign to eng-runtime oncall.

metering-bot: NOTE metering-run=2026-02-11T21:04:31Z pipeline-stage=dedupe-check status=queued

alex_s: Thanks — scheduling a pairing with eng-runtime 10:00AM PT tomorrow to reproduce and discuss dedupe heuristic. I'll follow up in thread with customer credit decision. :thumbsup:
